_comment: Auto-generated from the live registry by generateNodeManifest.svelte.test.js (GEN_MANIFEST=1) / `pnpm manifest:gen`. Do not hand-edit. Consumed by the Chronobiology Handbook Node Reference.

nodes.description: Actogram (double-plotted activity over days).

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours, for this series. Required for the series to draw.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Number columns (usually activity), one or more, drawn day by day.

outputs.name: r*_tau
outputs.description: Period of this marker rule’s line, from its harmonic check, in hours. One value per series.

outputs.name: r*_phi
outputs.description: Phase of the rule’s line, in hours after the row start on the reference day. One value per series.

outputs.name: r*_r2
outputs.description: R² of the rule’s line against its fitted markers. One value per series.

outputs.name: r*_rmse
outputs.description: RMSE of the rule’s line against its markers, in hours. One value per series.

outputs.name: r*_n
outputs.description: Number of markers in the rule’s fit (0 when none). One value per series.

nodes.description: Boxplot summarising the distribution of a column by group, with optional violin (kernel density) overlay and jittered data points; the box can be hidden for a pure violin plot. Horizontal reference lines and bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Optional column of group labels (categories): one box per group. Empty: the whole y column is one box.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more: the values summarised. Blanks are skipped.

nodes.description: Circular phase plot: one or more phase columns on an adjustable-period clock, each a coloured group with its Rayleigh mean-resultant vector; optional rose wedges and a Watson-Williams equal-mean-direction test. Wiring an optional time column (hours or timestamp, folded by period) to a series plots it at its measurement time with radius = value instead, and the vector becomes an amplitude-weighted acrophase.

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Optional time column (or hours as numbers), folded onto the period. Wired: the values are measurements at their time of day. Empty: the values are phases.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, each a group: phases (hours, degrees or radians, as set) or, with a time column, measurements.

nodes.description: Coloured correlation matrix computed from the wired columns.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: Number columns, one per variable, two or more. Each pair is correlated on the rows where both have a value.

nodes.description: Autocorrelation / cross-correlation plot, with reference lines and shaded bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab.

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours, for this series. Required for the series to draw. Lags are in hours.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, each analysed and drawn against this series’ time.

outputs.name: peak_lag
outputs.description: Lag of the first clear peak after lag 0, in hours. One value per series.

outputs.name: peak_correlation
outputs.description: Autocorrelation r at that peak, -1 to 1. One value per series.

nodes.description: Continuous wavelet transform (scalogram): power as a function of BOTH time and period, so a rhythm that changes period or strength over the record is visible where a periodogram would only show a time-average. Morlet/Paul/DOG wavelets, Torrence & Compo (1998) normalisation, with the cone of influence drawn (values outside it are edge artefacts) and an optional ridge showing the dominant period at each moment. Horizontal reference lines and bands on the period axis (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab. Requires uniformly sampled data.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: One number column to transform. The plot shows one series; a new wire replaces it.

nodes.description: Fourier analysis (FFT) spectrum of a time-series, with reference lines and shaded bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab; vertical positions are periods in hours, drawn at 1/period when the axis shows frequency.

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours, for this series. Required for the series to draw.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, each analysed and drawn against this series’ time.

outputs.name: peak_period
outputs.description: Period of the highest peak inside the axis limits (else the highest overall), in hours. One value per series.

outputs.name: peak_frequency
outputs.description: Frequency of that peak, in cycles per hour. One value per series.

outputs.name: peak_magnitude
outputs.description: Amplitude of that peak, in y units. One value per series.

nodes.description: Histogram of a column, with reference lines and shaded bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is its own histogram. Time columns are refused.

nodes.description: Mean ± SEM overlay: per-group mean marker with standard-error whiskers, with horizontal reference lines and bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Optional column of group labels: one mean and SEM per group. Empty: the whole y column is one group.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more: the values averaged.

nodes.description: Scatterplot matrix (pairs.panels): histograms on the diagonal, scatter + fit above, correlation below.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: Number columns, one per variable; every pair gets a scatter panel.

nodes.description: Periodogram (Lomb-Scargle / chi-squared) of a time-series, with reference lines and shaded bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab, e.g. a line at 24 h or at its own peak_period, or a 20 to 28 h band.

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours, for this series. Required for the series to draw.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, each analysed and drawn against this series’ time.

outputs.name: peak_period
outputs.description: Period of the highest peak inside the axis limits (else the highest overall), in hours. One value per series.

outputs.name: peak_power
outputs.description: Power at the peak: unitless for Lomb-Scargle, Qp for Chi-squared, y units for Enright. One value per series.

outputs.name: peak_pvalue
outputs.description: Family-wise p of the Chi-squared peak, corrected for every period tested. Blank for the other methods. One value per series.

nodes.description: Normal Q-Q plot: sample vs theoretical quantiles, with a quartile reference line and confidence envelope, plus your own reference lines and shaded bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, each compared with a normal distribution. Needs at least 3 values.

outputs.name: qq_r
outputs.description: Correlation of the Q-Q points with the normal line, up to 1 (1 is perfectly normal), one value per series. Blank for constant data or n under 3.

outputs.name: qq_n
outputs.description: Number of values used. One value per series.

nodes.description: Scatterplot of one column versus another, with reference lines and shaded bands (wired or typed) from its Overlays tab.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Time, number or category column for this series’ x axis.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, plotted against this series’ x.

nodes.description: Tabular display of wired columns, a plot's computed data, or an analysis node's results (stats, permutations).
Add a constant or column to the input column.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A number column, or a time column (the value added is then a duration).

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input plus the value, row by row. Same length and type; blanks stay blank.

nodes.description: Edit or substitute individual values in a column.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A column of any type.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: A copy of the input with the cells you typed changed, by row number.

nodes.description: Filter rows based on the values of another column.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A column of any type.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input with the rows that fail the conditions (tested on other columns) blanked. Same length.

nodes.description: FFT-based low-, high-, or band-pass filter over an evenly sampled series.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: An evenly sampled number column.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input after the low-, high- or band-pass FFT filter (cutoffs as fractions of the Nyquist frequency), in its own units. Blanks stay blank.

nodes.description: Multiply the input column by a constant or another column.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A number column.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input times the value, row by row. Same length; blanks stay blank.

nodes.description: Normalize the column to a chosen range or by a reference value.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A number column.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input rescaled (z-score, min-max, robust median and MAD, or unit vector), with no units. Blanks stay blank.

nodes.description: Detect and remove outliers from the column.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A number column.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input with outliers (by z-score or IQR fences) blanked. Same length; with fewer than 4 values it passes through.

nodes.description: Remove a fitted trend (linear, polynomial, etc.) from the column.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A number column. The trend runs along the x column chosen in the panel, else the row number.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input minus its fitted trend, in its own units (or a sliding z-score). Unchanged where the fit is refused.

nodes.description: Find a specific value in the column and replace it with another (e.g. swap a missing-data code like −999 for a different value).

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: A column of any type except time.

outputs.name: output
outputs.description: The input with every cell equal to the find value replaced. Same length and type.

nodes.description: Average daily profile: fold a series onto one period and show the per-bin mean (± SEM).

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. The period is in its units. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more. Each is folded onto the period and averaged into one profile.

outputs.name: avgprofx
outputs.description: Centre of each profile bin, in hours after that series’ first sample, across one period.

outputs.name: avgprof_*
outputs.description: Mean profile over one period: each day is averaged within the bin first, then the day means are averaged. In y units; blank for an empty bin.

outputs.name: avgprofsem_*
outputs.description: Standard error of the profile mean: the SD of the day means over the square root of the number of days. Blank with fewer than 2 days in the bin.

nodes.description: Bin time-series values into regular intervals and aggregate per bin.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Bins are in its units; custom edges need numbers. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Columns to bin, one or more. Rows with a blank x or y are dropped.

outputs.name: binnedx
outputs.description: Start (left edge) of each bin. A time column for a time x, else numbers. Points before the first bin are dropped.

outputs.name: binnedy_*
outputs.description: y summarised per bin by the function in the panel (mean by default; median, min, max, SD or count). Blank for an empty bin, except count, which is 0.

nodes.description: Enter data by hand, or paste CSV/JSON.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The values typed or pasted in. Numbers when every filled cell is a number, else categories; empty cells stay blank.

nodes.description: Tests for categorical data: chi-squared independence of two variables (contingency table), chi-squared goodness-of-fit against a uniform expectation, or Fisher's exact test for small 2x2 tables. Reports an effect size (Cramer's V, Cohen's w, or the odds ratio with a confidence interval) alongside the p-value.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One column of categories (or counts for goodness of fit). The first group, the row variable, or the only column tested. Required.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: One column of categories: the second group or the column variable. Needed for independence and Fisher; ignored for goodness of fit.

outputs.name: statistic
outputs.description: Chi-square (χ²), one value for the node. Blank for Fisher, which has no test statistic.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: p of the test, one value for the node (Fisher: exact, with the alternative set in the panel).

outputs.name: df
outputs.description: Degrees of freedom, one value for the node. Blank for Fisher.

outputs.name: effectSize
outputs.description: Effect size, one value for the node: Cramér's V (independence), Cohen's w (goodness of fit) or the conditional odds ratio (Fisher).

outputs.name: ciLow
outputs.description: Lower end of the exact 95% interval of the Fisher odds ratio, one value for the node. Blank for chi-square.

outputs.name: ciHigh
outputs.description: Upper end of the exact 95% interval of the Fisher odds ratio, one value for the node. Blank for chi-square.

nodes.description: Circadian Function Index (0–1) summarising rest-activity rhythm robustness from nonparametric IS, IV and RA (Ortiz-Tudela et al. 2010).

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns (usually activity), one or more.

outputs.name: CFI
outputs.description: Mean of IS, (2 - IV) / 2 and RA, each clamped to 0 to 1. Higher is a stronger rhythm; blank if a part is missing. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: IS
outputs.description: Interdaily stability, 0 to 1: how alike the days are. Higher is more stable. Not clamped. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: IV
outputs.description: Intradaily variability, about 0 to 2: how fragmented the rhythm is within a day. Higher is more fragmented. Not clamped. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: RA
outputs.description: Relative amplitude, (M10 - L5) / (M10 + L5): 0 to 1 for non-negative data. Not clamped. One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Gather several columns into one node, row by row (by position), with optional row-wise aggregates.

inputs.name: colIds
inputs.description: Columns of any type, one or more, to gather into this node. Required.

outputs.name: outCols
outputs.description: A copy of each wired column, after any steps set in the panel, keeping its type.

nodes.description: Apply a per-column aggregate function (mean, sum, etc.) across rows or groups.

inputs.name: xsIN
inputs.description: Columns, one or more, combined row by row. Required.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: One value per row from the chosen function across the columns (add, average, min, max, SD or percentile). As long as the first column.

nodes.description: Curate a live subset of columns by name/label and reuse it as one wire.

inputs.name: colsIN
inputs.description: Candidate columns of any type, one or more. The set keeps those whose name or group label contains the match text.

outputs.name: set
outputs.description: A live set of the matching columns down one wire. Connects only to an input that takes one or more columns (marked *).

nodes.description: Pairwise correlation matrix (Pearson or Spearman) across the wired columns, with normality-based auto method choice.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, two or more. Every pair is correlated, using rows where both have a value.

outputs.name: var_i
outputs.description: Name of the first column of each pair, one row per pair.

outputs.name: var_j
outputs.description: Name of the second column of each pair, one row per pair.

outputs.name: r
outputs.description: Correlation r of the pair (Pearson or Spearman), -1 to 1. Blank with fewer than 2 rows or no variance.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: Per-test p of each pair, not corrected for the number of pairs.

outputs.name: padj
outputs.description: Holm-adjusted p across all the pairs (family-wise).

outputs.name: n
outputs.description: Number of rows where both columns have a value, per pair.

outputs.name: ciLow
outputs.description: Lower end of the 95% interval of r, per pair. Blank with fewer than 4 rows.

outputs.name: ciHigh
outputs.description: Upper end of the 95% interval of r, per pair. Blank with fewer than 4 rows.

outputs.name: significant
outputs.description: 1 when the Holm-adjusted p is below alpha, else 0, per pair.

nodes.description: Fit a cosinor model (period, amplitude, acrophase) to the column.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Periods and phases come out in its units. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A column with too few rows for the model is skipped with a warning.

outputs.name: cosinorx
outputs.description: x of the fitted curves: the input rows with both x and y, or the output x set in the panel. Time for a time x, else numbers.

outputs.name: cosinory_*
outputs.description: The fitted cosinor (all harmonics, or all cosines for a free period), at the fit x rows, in y units. Shorter than the input when y has blanks.

outputs.name: resid_*
outputs.description: Observed y minus the fitted value at every input row, in y units. Same length as the input; blank where x or y is blank.

outputs.name: period
outputs.description: Fitted period of the first cosine, in hours (x units for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: mesor
outputs.description: MESOR: the rhythm-adjusted mean of the fit, in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: amplitude
outputs.description: Half the peak-to-trough range of the fitted cosine, in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: amplitude_ciLow
outputs.description: Lower end of the CI (the level set in the panel, 95% by default). Harmonic 1 amplitude; fixed period only. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: amplitude_ciHigh
outputs.description: Upper end of the CI (the level set in the panel, 95% by default). Harmonic 1 amplitude; fixed period only. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: acrophase_ciLow
outputs.description: Lower end of the CI (the level set in the panel, 95% by default). Harmonic 1 peak time; blank for a free period or no clear rhythm. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: acrophase_ciHigh
outputs.description: Upper end of the CI (the level set in the panel, 95% by default). Harmonic 1 peak time; blank for a free period or no clear rhythm. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: acrophase
outputs.description: Time of the fitted peak, in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: rsquared
outputs.description: R²: the share of the variance in y that the fit explains, 0 to 1. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: p of the zero-amplitude F-test (is there a rhythm). Fixed period only. Not corrected across series. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: perm_pvalue
outputs.description: Permutation-test p: the share of fits to shuffled data as good as the real one. Blank unless the test is on. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: bathyphase
outputs.description: Time of the fitted trough (half a period after the peak), in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: phase_angle
outputs.description: Peak time minus the reference time set in the panel, in hours (x units for a number x), within half a period. Positive: the peak is later. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: amplitude_h1
outputs.description: Amplitude of harmonic 1 alone, in y units. Same as the amplitude unless there are more harmonics. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: acrophase_h1
outputs.description: Peak time of harmonic 1 alone, in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: bathyphase_h1
outputs.description: Trough time of harmonic 1 alone, in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Cross-correlogram of two series: the correlation at each lag, with the peak lag revealing the delay between them.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: Series A: one number column. Rows pair with series B by position, so both should be evenly sampled. Required.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Series B: one number column, paired with A row by row. Required.

outputs.name: lag
outputs.description: Lag in samples (rows), from -max to +max lag, one row per lag. Positive means A leads B.

outputs.name: correlation
outputs.description: Correlation r of A with B shifted by that lag, -1 to 1, one row per lag.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: p of the prewhitened correlation at that lag, one row per lag. Per-lag: not corrected for testing many lags.

nodes.description: Find when a rule over one or more series becomes sustainedly true: conditions against typed values or wired scalar thresholds, combined as OR of AND-groups, with a persistence requirement. Outputs every crossing time, their count, and a 0/1 breach series.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: Optional time or number column. Wired: persistence is in its units (hours for time). Empty: persistence counts samples.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, that the rule tests. All must be the same length.

inputs.name: thresholdIN
inputs.description: Optional columns whose first value is a cutoff a rule can use instead of a typed number.

outputs.name: breach
outputs.description: 1 where the rule holds, else 0, one row per input row. Blank where a tested series is blank.

outputs.name: crossing
outputs.description: Where each crossing fired (the rule held for the persistence time): the x value, a time when x is time, or the row number (from 0) without x.

outputs.name: count
outputs.description: Number of crossings, one value for the node.

nodes.description: Per-column summary statistics (mean, median, sd, min/max, quartiles, skewness, kurtosis).

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more. One row of statistics per column; blanks are ignored.

outputs.name: variable
outputs.description: Name of each input column, one row per column.

outputs.name: n
outputs.description: Number of values (blanks left out), one row per column.

outputs.name: mean
outputs.description: Mean, in the column’s units, one row per column.

outputs.name: median
outputs.description: Median, in the column’s units, one row per column.

outputs.name: sd
outputs.description: Sample standard deviation (n - 1), in the column’s units.

outputs.name: min
outputs.description: Smallest value, one row per column.

outputs.name: max
outputs.description: Largest value, one row per column.

outputs.name: range
outputs.description: Largest minus smallest value, one row per column.

outputs.name: q1
outputs.description: 25th percentile (linear interpolation), one row per column.

outputs.name: q3
outputs.description: 75th percentile (linear interpolation), one row per column.

outputs.name: iqr
outputs.description: Interquartile range, Q3 minus Q1, one row per column.

outputs.name: skewness
outputs.description: Skewness (bias-corrected), no units. Blank with fewer than 3 values.

outputs.name: kurtosis
outputs.description: Excess kurtosis (0 for a normal distribution), no units. Blank with fewer than 4 values.

nodes.description: Fit a double-logistic curve to the column (useful for phenology / on-off transitions).

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A column with fewer than 4 usable rows is skipped.

outputs.name: dlogx
outputs.description: x of the fitted curves: the input rows with both x and y, or the output x set in the panel. Time for a time x, else numbers.

outputs.name: dlogy_*
outputs.description: The fitted double logistic (a rise to a bout and a fall back, each cycle), at the fit x rows, in y units. Shorter than the input when y has blanks.

outputs.name: resid_*
outputs.description: Observed y minus the fitted value at every input row, in y units. Same length as the input; blank where x or y is blank.

outputs.name: perm_pvalue
outputs.description: Permutation-test p: the share of fits to shuffled data as good as the real one. Blank unless the test is on. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: r2
outputs.description: R²: the share of the variance in y that the fit explains, 0 to 1. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: rmse
outputs.description: Root mean square error, sqrt(SS / n), in y units. One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Adjust a column of p-values for multiple comparisons and flag which survive. Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR under independence or positive dependence), Benjamini-Yekutieli (FDR under arbitrary dependence), Holm and Bonferroni (family-wise error). Missing p-values stay missing and are excluded from the count, so a test that failed to run never tightens the correction on the ones that did.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One column of raw p-values (for example a pvalue output). Values outside 0 to 1, blanks and text are left out. Required.

outputs.name: padj
outputs.description: Adjusted p for each input row (false discovery rate or family-wise, by method). Blank where the input p is unusable.

outputs.name: reject
outputs.description: 1 when the adjusted p is below alpha, else 0, for each input row.

nodes.description: Fit a named waveform model to the column: cosinor, rectangular wave, or double logistic. Use it to compare different waveform shapes on the same series without rewiring; the fit quality (R2, RMSE, permutation p) and the chosen model’s parameters are wireable metric output ports, like the dedicated Cosinor, Rectangular Wave and Double Logistic nodes.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Periods, phases and rates come out in its units. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A column with too few rows for the model is skipped with a warning.

outputs.name: fitx
outputs.description: x of the fitted curves: the input rows with both x and y, or the output x set in the panel. Time for a time x, else numbers.

outputs.name: fity_*
outputs.description: The fitted model (cosinor, rectangular wave or double logistic), at the fit x rows, in y units. Shorter than the input when y has blanks.

outputs.name: resid_*
outputs.description: Observed y minus the fitted value at every input row, in y units. Same length as the input; blank where x or y is blank.

outputs.name: permstats_*
outputs.description: The statistic (R² or RMSE) of every permuted fit, one row per permutation. Empty unless the permutation test is on.

outputs.name: r2
outputs.description: R²: the share of the variance in y that the fit explains, 0 to 1. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: rmse
outputs.description: Residual standard error, sqrt(SS / (n - p)), in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: rmse_n
outputs.description: Root mean square error, sqrt(SS / n), in y units. Fixed-period cosinor only, beside its residual SE. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: perm_pvalue
outputs.description: Permutation-test p: the share of fits to shuffled data as good as the real one. Blank unless the test is on. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: period
outputs.description: The fixed period the cosine was fitted at, in hours (x units for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: mesor
outputs.description: MESOR: the rhythm-adjusted mean of the fit, in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: amplitude
outputs.description: Half the peak-to-trough range of the fitted cosine, in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: acrophase
outputs.description: Time of the fitted peak, in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: amplitude_h1
outputs.description: Amplitude of harmonic 1 alone, in y units (cosinor model). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: acrophase_h1
outputs.description: Peak time of harmonic 1 alone, in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x) (cosinor model). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: duty_cycle
outputs.description: Fraction of each cycle at the high (active) level, 0 to 1. Rectangular wave, or a periodic double logistic. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: kappa
outputs.description: Edge sharpness of the rectangular wave; larger is more square. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: onset
outputs.description: Time the activity bout rises (double logistic), in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: offset
outputs.description: Time the activity bout falls (double logistic), in hours after the first sample (x units from 0 for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: k1
outputs.description: Steepness of the rise (double logistic), per hour (per x unit for a number x). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: k2
outputs.description: Steepness of the fall (double logistic), per hour (per x unit for a number x). One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Compute a new column from a user-supplied formula referencing other columns.

inputs.name: tokens
inputs.description: The columns the formula uses. The first one sets the number of rows. Required.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The formula worked out row by row, as numbers. Blank where any input is blank or the result is not finite.

nodes.description: Compare statistics between groups defined by another column.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One column of group labels (text or numbers, read as categories). Empty: each y column is its own group, compared with the others.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more: the values compared across the groups. Each is tested separately.

outputs.name: statistic
outputs.description: The test statistic (t, F, U or H, by method), one value per wired y column, or one when the y columns are the groups.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: Omnibus p of the test, one value per wired y column; not corrected across y columns.

outputs.name: effectSize
outputs.description: Effect size, one value per wired y column: Cohen's d (t-test), η² (ANOVA), r (Mann-Whitney) or ε² (Kruskal-Wallis).

nodes.description: Fill missing values or resample a series onto a regular grid by interpolation (linear, nearest, or cubic spline).

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, to fill in or resample. Each needs at least one row with both x and y.

outputs.name: interpx
outputs.description: Fill mode: a copy of the input x. Resample mode: an even grid, one row per step across the data. Time for a time x.

outputs.name: interpy_*
outputs.description: y at each output x, filled by linear, nearest or cubic spline interpolation. Blank outside the range of known x (no extrapolation).

nodes.description: Put every row of two datasets (A and B) on one time column, sorted by time; same-named value columns share a column.

inputs.name: aTimeIN
inputs.description: Time of dataset A: a time column, or numbers. Wire a time for both A and B (rows interleave in time order) or for neither (B is stacked under A).

inputs.name: aValuesIN
inputs.description: Columns of dataset A, one or more. Each pairs with the B column of the same name.

inputs.name: bTimeIN
inputs.description: Time of dataset B, the same kind as time A (both time, or both numbers). Leave both times empty to stack B under A.

inputs.name: bValuesIN
inputs.description: Columns of dataset B, one or more. A B column with no A partner of the same name gets its own output.

outputs.name: jointime
outputs.description: Every A and B time in order (A first on ties). Only when both times are wired; no rows are merged.

outputs.name: joined_*
outputs.description: A joined column: A values on A rows and B values on B rows for a pair, blank on the other dataset’s rows when unpaired.

outputs.name: source
outputs.description: Which dataset each row came from (the group names, or A and B).

nodes.description: Model a binary outcome from one or more predictors: coefficients, odds ratios with 95% CIs, Wald p-values, and model fit (pseudo-R², LR test).

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: The outcome: one column of 0 and 1 (or two text levels). Any other column gives a "not binary" warning.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: Predictors: number columns, one or more. Rows missing the outcome or any predictor are dropped.

outputs.name: term
outputs.description: Name of each model term, one row per term; the first is the intercept.

outputs.name: coef
outputs.description: Coefficient of each term, on the log-odds scale.

outputs.name: se
outputs.description: Standard error of each coefficient.

outputs.name: z
outputs.description: Wald z of each coefficient (coefficient / standard error).

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: Wald p of each term; not corrected across terms.

outputs.name: oddsRatio
outputs.description: Odds ratio of each term, e to the coefficient.

outputs.name: ciLow
outputs.description: Lower end of the 95% interval of the odds ratio, per term.

outputs.name: ciHigh
outputs.description: Upper end of the 95% interval of the odds ratio, per term.

outputs.name: outcome
outputs.description: The 0/1 outcome actually used, one row per input row (blank for dropped rows).

outputs.name: eta
outputs.description: Linear predictor (log-odds) for each input row.

outputs.name: fitted
outputs.description: Fitted probability that the outcome is 1, for each input row.

nodes.description: Pivot a long-format table into wide format.

inputs.name: categoryIN
inputs.description: One column of labels: each distinct label becomes its own value column. Required.

inputs.name: timeIN
inputs.description: One time (or number) column; rows with a blank time are dropped. Required.

inputs.name: valueIN
inputs.description: One column of the values to spread out. Required.

outputs.name: time
outputs.description: The distinct times, sorted, one row each.

outputs.name: value_*
outputs.description: The values of one label at each time. Blank where that label has no row; a repeated label and time keeps the last value.

nodes.description: Compute a rolling-window analysis across the column.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Window size and step are in its units. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A window with fewer than 3 usable rows gives a blank cell.

outputs.name: stats_*
outputs.description: One column per wired y column and statistic of the chosen analysis, one row per window. Blank for a window without enough data.

nodes.description: Nonparametric rest-activity variables (IS, IV, RA, M10/L5), robust to non-sinusoidal rhythms.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: Time column, or numbers read as hours. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns (usually activity), one or more. Each is binned into epochs and folded onto the period.

outputs.name: npcrax
outputs.description: Centre of each epoch of the average day, in hours after the first sample. Taken from the first y column.

outputs.name: npcray_*
outputs.description: The average day: the mean of each epoch across days, in y units. Blank for an empty epoch.

outputs.name: IS
outputs.description: Interdaily stability, 0 to 1: how alike the days are. Higher is more stable. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: IV
outputs.description: Intradaily variability, about 0 to 2: how fragmented the rhythm is within a day. Higher is more fragmented. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: RA
outputs.description: Relative amplitude, (M10 - L5) / (M10 + L5): 0 to 1 for non-negative data. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: M10
outputs.description: Mean of the most active 10 h of the average day, in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: L5
outputs.description: Mean of the least active 5 h of the average day, in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: M10onset
outputs.description: Start of the most active 10 h window, in hours after the first sample, folded onto the period. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: L5onset
outputs.description: Start of the least active 5 h window, in hours after the first sample, folded onto the period. One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Test each wired column for normality (Shapiro-Wilk by default, or D’Agostino-Pearson / Jarque-Bera), reporting the statistic, p-value and a verdict.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more. One row of results per column.

outputs.name: variable
outputs.description: Name of each input column, one row per column.

outputs.name: statistic
outputs.description: Test statistic: Shapiro-Wilk W, D’Agostino K² or Jarque-Bera JB, by method.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: p of the normality test, per column. Blank if n is too small (or above 5000 for Shapiro-Wilk).

outputs.name: n
outputs.description: Number of values tested, per column.

outputs.name: normal
outputs.description: 1 when p is at least alpha (normality not rejected), 0 when rejected.

nodes.description: Generate a column of random values.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Random numbers (uniform, gaussian, exponential or 0/1 bernoulli), rounded to 2 decimals. The seed makes them repeatable.

nodes.description: Circular statistics on phase/angle columns: the Rayleigh uniformity test (R, z, p, acrophase) per column, with an optional Watson-Williams equal-mean-direction test (F, p) across columns. Wiring an optional time column (hours or timestamp, folded by period) switches to an amplitude-weighted mean vector/acrophase; without it, values are treated as raw angles.

inputs.name: timeIN
inputs.description: Optional time column (or hours as numbers). Wired: each y value becomes a weight at its time folded onto the period. Empty: the y columns hold the angles.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more, each a group: angles in the unit set in the panel, or weights when a time column is wired.

outputs.name: R
outputs.description: Mean vector length, 0 to 1: 0 is spread evenly round the cycle, 1 is all at one phase. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: z
outputs.description: Rayleigh z = n·R². Blank when a time column is wired (weighted mode). One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: Rayleigh test p (are the phases clustered); not corrected across columns. Blank when a time column is wired. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: F
outputs.description: Watson-Williams F comparing the mean directions of the y columns: one value for the node. Blank when the test is off, weighted, or with fewer than 2 groups.

outputs.name: ww_pvalue
outputs.description: Watson-Williams p (do the groups share a mean direction): one value for the node. Blank when the test is off, weighted, or with fewer than 2 groups.

outputs.name: acrophase
outputs.description: Mean direction, as hours of a cycle of the period set in the panel (24 by default), 0 up to the period. One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Fit a rectangular (square) wave model with adjustable duty cycle.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A column with fewer than 4 usable rows is skipped.

outputs.name: rectwavex
outputs.description: x of the fitted curves: the input rows with both x and y, or the output x set in the panel. Time for a time x, else numbers.

outputs.name: rectwavey_*
outputs.description: The fitted rectangular wave (a smoothed square wave), at the fit x rows, in y units. Shorter than the input when y has blanks.

outputs.name: resid_*
outputs.description: Observed y minus the fitted value at every input row, in y units. Same length as the input; blank where x or y is blank.

outputs.name: perm_pvalue
outputs.description: Permutation-test p: the share of fits to shuffled data as good as the real one. Blank unless the test is on. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: r2
outputs.description: R²: the share of the variance in y that the fit explains, 0 to 1. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: rmse
outputs.description: Root mean square error, sqrt(SS / n), in y units. One value per wired y column.

nodes.description: Run rhythmicity statistics over the column.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Periods and lags come out in its units. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A column with fewer than 3 usable rows gives blank results.

outputs.name: rhythmicityx
outputs.description: Trial period of each point of the spectrum, in hours (x units for a number x).

outputs.name: rhythmicityy_*
outputs.description: The spectrum or correlogram values for this y column.

outputs.name: stat_*
outputs.description: A peak statistic, one value per wired y column: period, power or p; frequency or magnitude; or lag and r, by analysis.

nodes.description: Create a numeric or time sequence column.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: An evenly spaced sequence: numbers from the start in equal steps, or times from the start time, one step (in hours) apart.

nodes.description: Generate a synthetic time series from a square-wave (active/rest) rhythm plus noise.

outputs.name: time
outputs.description: Time of each simulated sample, every sampling interval from the start time.

outputs.name: values
outputs.description: The simulated signal: a square wave (the amplitude while active, 1 at rest) with optional noise, one value per time.

nodes.description: Smooth a column using LOESS, moving average, Savitzky-Golay, or Whittaker-Eilers.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. A column with fewer than 3 usable rows is skipped.

outputs.name: smoothedx
outputs.description: x of the smoothed points: the rows with both x and y, sorted by x. A time column for a time x.

outputs.name: smoothedy_*
outputs.description: Smoothed y at the smoothed x rows (Whittaker, moving average, Savitzky-Golay or LOESS), in y units. Not aligned with the input rows.

outputs.name: resid_*
outputs.description: Observed minus smoothed y at the smoothed x rows, in y units. Lines up with the smoothed x output, not with the input.

nodes.description: Sort rows by a chosen column, keeping the selected columns aligned (ascending or descending).

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Columns, one or more, kept row-aligned. The one chosen in the panel (the first by default) is the sort key.

outputs.name: sortedy_*
outputs.description: The column reordered by the sort key, so rows stay together. Blank keys go last; a column of a different length is passed through unsorted.

nodes.description: Split a column or table on a delimiter or group key.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time or number column the split points are read on (dates for time, numbers otherwise). Required.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Columns, one or more, to cut into segments.

outputs.name: segments
outputs.description: One column per wired y column and segment: full length, with values only between that segment’s split points.

nodes.description: Group derived stored values together for reuse.

outputs.name: category
outputs.description: Group name of each stored value (older sessions only).

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The stored values of every group (older sessions only).

nodes.description: Test rhythm strength against a surrogate null that PRESERVES the series' nuisance structure. Plain shuffling destroys autocorrelation, which makes the null far too easy to beat; block bootstrap and AR(1) red noise keep it. Phase-randomised and AAFT surrogates are not offered: they keep the power spectrum, rhythm included, so they cannot test whether a rhythm is there.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: One number column to test for a rhythm. Needs at least 8 rows; gaps longer than 3 samples are refused.

outputs.name: pvalue
outputs.description: Share of surrogate series whose statistic reaches the observed one, one value for the node. The smallest possible p is 1 / (surrogates + 1).

outputs.name: observed
outputs.description: The test statistic on the real data: the largest FFT amplitude in the period band, in y units. One value for the node.

nodes.description: Turn a column into a 0/1 (binary) column at a user-set cutoff, e.g. to make a binary outcome for logistic regression.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One number column to compare with the threshold. Required.

outputs.name: binary
outputs.description: 1 where the value meets the comparison (for example at or above the threshold), else 0. Same length as the input; blank where the input is blank.

nodes.description: Fit a slow, non-oscillatory trend by least squares (linear, polynomial, exponential or logarithmic) and store the fitted curve with its R2, RMSE and coefficients. Use it to describe or remove baseline drift, growth or decay before rhythm analysis.

inputs.name: xIN
inputs.description: One time column (as hours from the first sample) or number column. A time x starts at 0, so rates are per hour. Required; nothing runs until it is wired.

inputs.name: yIN
inputs.description: Number columns, one or more; each is analysed on its own. The exponential model needs y above 0; the logarithmic model needs x above 0.

outputs.name: trendx
outputs.description: x of the fitted curves: the input rows with both x and y, or the output x set in the panel. Time for a time x, else numbers.

outputs.name: trendy_*
outputs.description: The fitted trend, at the fit x rows, in y units. Shorter than the input when y has blanks.

outputs.name: resid_*
outputs.description: Observed y minus the fitted value at every input row, in y units. Same length as the input; blank where x or y is blank.

outputs.name: r2
outputs.description: R² on the original y scale, 0 to 1. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: rmse
outputs.description: Root mean square error, sqrt(SS / n), in y units. One value per wired y column.

outputs.name: coef_*
outputs.description: A trend coefficient, one value per wired y column: slope and intercept, a and b, or c0 to cN, by model.

nodes.description: Pivot a wide-format table into long format.

inputs.name: timeIN
inputs.description: One time (or number) column shared by the value columns. Required.

inputs.name: valueColIds
inputs.description: Value columns, one or more, to stack into one. Required.

outputs.name: time
outputs.description: The time of each stacked row (the input times repeated for every value column).

outputs.name: category
outputs.description: Name of the column each stacked value came from, as the app shows it.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The stacked values. Rows with a blank time or value are left out.
